mainTopic: Teachings on תלמידי חכמים, the growing curse since the חורבן, wartime decrees, and qualities lost with the deaths of great sages
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching: when the young children of רשעים die early, that loss already counts as their fathers' punishment. Next comes a series of sayings from רבי אילעא בר יברכיה about תלמידי חכמים. The תפילות of דוד and חבקוק saved them from poverty. Scholars who walk together must talk in Torah. Scholars who fight over הלכה bring harm on each other. Then come the rewards for learning in poverty: one's תפילה is answered, one sees the שכינה, and even the heavenly פרגוד stays open. The גמרא goes back to the משנה. רבא shows that each day since the חורבן is worse than the one before, and that the world survives through the קדושה דסידרא and יהא שמיה רבא. Two stories about fragrant dates and grandchildren show that love flows down the generations. A new משנה lists the wartime decrees and the qualities that ended when great sages died. The גמרא then brings רבי פנחס בן יאיר and רבי אליעזר הגדול on how society fell after the חורבן, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Young children who die take away their fathers' future punishment
steps.stepSummary: The young children of רשעים 'plunder' their fathers' judgment in the future. They argue before הקב״ה that their early death was already their fathers' punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: They plunder their fathers' judgment in the future. They say before Him: Master of the world, since You were going to punish them anyway, why did You blunt their teeth with us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that began before this section. It explains how the young children of רשעים 'plunder,' meaning wipe out, the judgment of their fathers לעתיד לבוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children argue that their fathers already suffered when the children died young. Punishing the fathers again later would be double punishment. So the children's death works as a כפרה that wipes away the fathers' judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: in the future, the World to Come
to punish, to collect payment for sins
You blunted (set on edge) their teeth, meaning You caused them pain

steps.confusionAlert: This text begins in the middle of a sentence. 'They' are the young children of the רשעים, who were spoken about just before this section.

phrases.english: who plunder their fathers' judgment in the future.
phrases.notes: 'Plunder' here means they wipe out the judgment their fathers would have faced.

phrases.english: They say before Him: Master of the world,
since You were going to punish them in the future,
why did You blunt their teeth with us?
phrases.notes: Literally 'with them,' meaning the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמְּבַזְבְּזִין דִּין אֲבִיהֶם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The early death of the children of רשעים serves as their fathers' punishment and cancels their future judgment.

steps.title: דוד's prayer saved ישראל from lowly jobs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא בר יברכיה says that without the תפילה of דוד, all of ישראל would be sellers of fat. He brings a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא בר יברכיה said: If not for the prayer of דוד, all of ישראל would be sellers of fat, as it says: 'Place, O ה׳, mastery for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new series of sayings by רבי אילעא בר יברכיה. The first one says that דוד's תפילה kept ישראל from having to work in lowly jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Selling fat' stands for a low, dirty job. דוד prayed that ה׳ give ישראל 'mastery,' meaning dignity and a respectable living. That prayer is why ישראל is not stuck in such work.

keyTerms.meaning: sellers of fat or grease, a lowly job

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a bar Yeverekhya said:
If not for the prayer of David,
all of Israel would be sellers of fat,
as it says: 'Place, O Lord, mastery for them.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 9:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא בַּר יְבֶרֶכְיָה: אִלְמָלֵא תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of sayings by one אמורא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's prayer gave ישראל dignified ways to earn a living.

steps.title: חבקוק's prayer saved תלמידי חכמים from sharing one cloak
steps.stepSummary: Without the תפילה of חבקוק, two תלמידי חכמים would have to cover themselves with one cloak while learning. This is learned by rereading a פסוק in חבקוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the prayer of חבקוק, two תלמידי חכמים would cover themselves with one cloak and learn Torah. The פסוק says 'in the midst of the years,' but read it as 'in the closeness of two.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second saying of רבי אילעא בר יברכיה. חבקוק's prayer saved תלמידי חכמים from extreme poverty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses an אל תקרא, a reread of the פסוק's words. 'בקרב שנים' (in the midst of the years) is read as 'בקרוב שנים' (two people pressed close together). חבקוק asked ה׳ to 'revive' this situation, meaning to cancel the decree of such poverty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'do not read' — a reread of the פסוק's words to learn a lesson

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a bar Yeverekhya said:
If not for the prayer of Habakkuk,
two Torah scholars would be
covering themselves with one cloak
and studying Torah,
as it says: 'Lord, I heard Your report and was afraid;
phrases.notes: חבקוק 3:2

phrases.english: Lord, revive Your work in the midst of the years.'
Do not read 'in the midst of the years,'
but rather 'in the closeness of two.'
phrases.notes: Same letters, read differently: two people squeezed together under one cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא בַּר יְבֶרֶכְיָה: אִלְמָלֵא תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבַקּוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second saying in the same series, with the same 'if not for the prayer of' pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חבקוק's prayer saved תלמידי חכמים from crushing poverty.

steps.title: Scholars walking together must speak Torah
steps.stepSummary: Two תלמידי חכמים who travel without speaking דברי תורה deserve to be burned. This is learned from אליהו and אלישע, who were talking when the fiery chariot came.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two תלמידי חכמים walking on the road with no Torah between them deserve to be burned in fire. The פסוק says: 'They were walking and talking, and behold a chariot of fire.' The reason they were saved is that there was talk; without talk, they would have deserved to be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third saying of רבי אילעא בר יברכיה. He teaches that תלמידי חכמים who travel together must fill their time with Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by inference. אליהו and אלישע were 'talking' when the chariot of fire appeared, and the fire only separated them without harming them. The גמרא reasons that the talking, which was Torah, protected them. Without it, they would have deserved to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: who are walking on the road
the reason is that there is

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a bar Yeverekhya said:
Two Torah scholars who are walking on the road
and there are no words of Torah between them —
they deserve to be burned in fire,
as it says: 'And as they were walking along and talking,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:11. 'They' are אליהו and אלישע.

phrases.english: behold, a chariot of fire, etc.'
The reason is that there was talking,
but if there had been no talking, they would have deserved to be burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא בַּר יְבֶרֶכְיָה: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third saying in the series; shifts from prayer to how scholars should behave
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars traveling together must talk in Torah; otherwise they deserve to be burned.

steps.title: Scholars who keep fighting over הלכה end up with one dead and one exiled
steps.stepSummary: Two תלמידי חכמים in one city who are not pleasant to each other about הלכה will end with one dying and the other going into exile. This is learned from the פסוק about a רוצח בשוגג, together with the idea that 'דעת' means Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two תלמידי חכמים who live in one city and are not pleasant to each other in הלכה: one dies and one goes into exile. The פסוק says: 'For a killer to flee there, who kills his neighbor without דעת,' and 'דעת' means only Torah, as it says: 'My people are destroyed for lack of דעת.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth saying of רבי אילעא בר יברכיה. Fighting between scholars over הלכה leads to death and exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. First, a פסוק about a killer who must flee to a city of refuge because he killed 'בבלי דעת,' without knowledge. Second, a פסוק in הושע shows that 'דעת' means Torah. So the פסוק is read as one scholar 'killing' the other through Torah disputes, which leaves one dead and the killer in exile.

keyTerms.meaning: they are not pleasant to each other

steps.whatToRemember: All four sayings of רבי אילעא בר יברכיה are about the worth of Torah and its learners. דוד's and חבקוק's prayers saved them from poverty. Scholars must speak Torah when they walk together. And they must be pleasant to each other in הלכה, or terrible things can happen.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a bar Yeverekhya said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַדָּרִין בְּעִיר אַחַת
phrases.english: Two Torah scholars who live in one city
and are not pleasant to each other in halakha —
one dies and one goes into exile,
as it says: 'For a killer to flee there,'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:42

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יִרְצַח אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בִּבְלִי דַעַת״,
phrases.english: 'who kills his neighbor without knowledge,'
and 'knowledge' means nothing but Torah,
as it says: 'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.'
phrases.notes: הושע 4:6

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא בַּר יְבֶרֶכְיָה: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַדָּרִין בְּעִיר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth saying in the series, again about two תלמידי חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars in one city who fight over הלכה bring about one's death and the other's exile.

steps.title: A Torah scholar who learns in poverty has his prayer answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא teaches that a תלמיד חכם who learns Torah under the pressure of poverty has his תפילה heard. He proves it from two פסוקים in ישעיהו that come one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, the son of רבי חייא, said: Any Torah scholar who learns Torah while living in hardship will have his prayer heard. The פסוק says that the people sitting in Zion will not cry, because ה׳ will answer their cry. The very next פסוק talks about 'scarce bread and limited water.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about the reward of a תלמיד חכם who learns even though he is poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק promises that ה׳ will answer 'the people in Zion', meaning those who sit and learn. The next פסוק mentions 'scarce bread and limited water', so the promise is about people who learn while living on very little. Reading the two פסוקים together shows that a poor person who keeps learning has his תפילה answered.

keyTerms.meaning: While under pressure, in poverty and hardship
And it is written right after it (the next פסוק)
Scarce bread and limited water, a picture of a poor life

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya, said:
Any Torah scholar who busies himself with Torah
while under pressure (of poverty) —
his prayer is heard,
as it says: "For a people shall dwell in Zion, in Jerusalem;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל:יט

phrases.english: you shall not weep at all;
He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry;
when He hears it, He will answer you."
And it is written right after it:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְנָתַן ה׳ לָכֶם לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ״.
phrases.english: "And ה׳ will give you scarce bread and limited water."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל:כ. This next פסוק is what shows the first one is talking about people living in poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching to the series of מימרות about תלמידי חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם who learns Torah in poverty has his תפילה answered.

steps.title: He is filled with the radiance of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that a poor scholar who learns is filled with the radiance of the שכינה, learned from the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: He is filled with the radiance of the שכינה, as the פסוק says, 'Your eyes will see your Teacher.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different, greater reward for the same poor תלמיד חכם, using the same פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that mentions 'scarce bread' goes on to say 'your eyes will see your Teacher.' רבי אבהו reads 'your Teacher' as ה׳. So the reward is not only that his תפילה is answered, but that he is 'filled' by the radiance of the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: They fill him, he is satisfied
The radiance of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu says:
He is filled with the radiance of the Divine Presence,
as it says: "And your eyes shall see your Teacher."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל:כ, the same פסוק that spoke about scarce bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different (greater) reward for the same person described in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor scholar who learns is filled with the radiance of the שכינה.

steps.title: Even the heavenly פרגוד is not closed before him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא goes further: even the curtain that hides the שכינה is not closed in front of this scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: Even the curtain is not locked in front of him, as the פסוק says, 'Your Teacher will no longer hide Himself.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third rabbi adds an even bigger reward for the same scholar, from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' ('even') shows he is building on רבי אבהו. Not only does the scholar see the radiance of the שכינה, but nothing stands between him and ה׳‎. 'יכנף' means hiding behind a covering, so 'He will no longer hide' means the curtain stays open for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A curtain; here, the heavenly curtain that hides the שכינה

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
Even the curtain is not locked before him,
phrases.notes: The פרגוד is the heavenly curtain that separates the שכינה from everyone else.

phrases.english: as it says: "And your Teacher shall no longer hide Himself."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל:כ

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: אַף אֵין הַפַּרְגּוֹד נִנְעָל בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אבהו with an even greater reward ('אף')
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the heavenly curtain is not closed before the poor scholar who learns.
steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of reward for learning in poverty: his תפילה is answered, he is filled with the radiance of the שכינה, and even the heavenly curtain stays open for him.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: since the בית המקדש was destroyed, no day is without a curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the name of רבי יהושע, so it can explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יהושע: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, there is no (day without a curse), and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by quoting a line from the משנה that it is about to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is argued here yet. The quote brings us back to the משנה's statement that every day since the חורבן carries a curse, and רבא will explain it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the quote continues as in the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אֵין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: From the day the Temple was destroyed, there is no, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה finishes the thought: there is no day without a curse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the scholar teachings and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, there is no day without a curse.

steps.title: רבא: each day is more cursed than the day before
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that each day is more cursed than the one before it, and brings a פסוק from the curses in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Every single day, its curse is greater than the day before it. As the פסוק says: 'In the morning you will say, if only it were evening, and in the evening you will say, if only it were morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the משנה: things don't just stay bad, they get worse every day. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said there is a curse every day. רבא adds that the curse grows from day to day. His proof is the פסוק where a person keeps wishing for a different time of day, but it is not yet clear how this shows things are getting worse, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Than that of the one before it

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם מְרוּבָּה קִלְלָתוֹ מִשֶּׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: Each and every day, its curse is greater than that of the one before it,
as it says: "In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening,'
phrases.notes: דברים כח:סז

phrases.english: and in the evening you will say, 'If only it were morning.'"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם מְרוּבָּה קִלְלָתוֹ מִשֶּׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and sharpens the משנה just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each day since the חורבן is more cursed than the day before it.

steps.title: Which morning is the verse talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which morning the person in the פסוק is wishing for in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which morning does he mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about רבא's פסוק, setting up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To see how the פסוק proves that each day is worse, we must know which morning the person longs for in the evening. The answer will decide whether the פסוק supports רבא.

phrases.english: Which morning?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי בֹּקֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the פסוק רבא brought
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'morning' wished for in the evening is the coming morning or the one that already passed.

steps.title: It can't mean tomorrow morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that he is wishing for tomorrow morning, because nobody knows what tomorrow will bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means tomorrow morning, does he know what it will be like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, that he wants tomorrow morning, and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person only longs for a time if he knows it is better. Tomorrow morning is unknown, so there is no reason to long for it. So 'morning' in the פסוק cannot mean the coming morning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing a possibility that will be rejected)
Does he know what will be?

phrases.english: If you say it means tomorrow's morning,
does he know what it will be like?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בֹּקֶר דְּלִמְחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to the question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No one knows what tomorrow holds, so there is no reason to long for it.

steps.title: It means the morning that already passed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that in the evening he longs for the morning that already passed, which proves each part of the day is worse than the one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the morning that has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer: he wishes he could go back to this morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If in the evening he wishes to go back to the morning, the morning was better than the evening. Things keep getting worse as time goes on, and this proves רבא's point that each day is more cursed than the one before.

phrases.english: Rather, the one that has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּחֲלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after rejecting the first option
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'morning' is the one that already passed; he longs to go back to it, so time keeps getting worse.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא proves the world gets worse each day: in the evening a person longs for the morning that already passed.

steps.title: Then how does the world keep existing?
steps.stepSummary: If things keep getting worse every day, the גמרא asks what keeps the world going at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, why does the world keep existing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty that comes out of רבא's teaching: with curses growing every day, why hasn't the world fallen apart?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. If every day is worse than the last, there must be something good holding the world up, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

phrases.english: But then, why does the world keep existing?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, עָלְמָא אַמַּאי קָא מִקַּיַּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a difficulty based on the conclusion that every day is worse
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's teaching that every day is more cursed than the one before
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the curses keep growing, the world should not be able to survive; something must be holding it up.

steps.title: The world stands on the קדושה דסידרא and the יהא שמיה רבא after אגדתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the world survives because of the קדושה דסידרא and the יהא שמיה רבא said after learning אגדתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands on the קדושה said in the order of prayers, and on the 'יהא שמיה רבא' said after learning אגדתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: two special forms of praising ה׳ are what hold the world up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are moments when people praise ה׳ together while learning. The קדושה דסידרא is said with its translation, so it joins prayer and learning. The יהא שמיה רבא after אגדתא is the קדיש said after a public lesson. These keep the world going even as the curses grow.

keyTerms.meaning: The קדושה said in the order of prayers (in ובא לציון)
'May His great Name be blessed', the response in קדיש
אגדה, the non-legal teachings of Torah

phrases.english: On the Kedusha of the order (of prayers),
phrases.notes: This is the קדושה in ובא לציון, said together with its Aramaic translation.

phrases.english: and on the "May His great Name be blessed" said after Aggada,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְסִידְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of how the world survives
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names the merit that holds up the world despite the growing curses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With curses increasing every day, the world should have nothing left to hold it up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The world is held up by the קדושה דסידרא and the יהא שמיה רבא said after learning אגדתא.

steps.title: Proof from איוב: where there are 'orders', light appears from darkness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in איוב that calls a dark land 'without orders', and infers that where there are 'orders' the land shines out of the darkness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'A land of gloom like darkness itself, of the shadow of death, without orders.' So if there are 'orders', it will shine out of the darkness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a land of total darkness as one 'without orders' (סדרים). The גמרא reads this the other way around: if there are סדרים, the land comes out of the darkness. 'סדרים' hints at the 'סידרא', the order of prayers and learning, from the answer in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Orders; here, the set order of prayers and learning

phrases.english: as it says: "A land of gloom like darkness itself,
phrases.notes: איוב י:כב

phrases.english: of the shadow of death, and without orders."
So if there are orders —
it will shine out of the darkness.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֶרֶץ עֵיפָתָה כְּמוֹ אֹפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 15
steps.raayaObject: That the world is held up by the 'סידרא', the set order of prayer and learning
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב י:כב, read in reverse: where there are סדרים, the land shines out of darkness
steps.whatToRemember: Even though every day since the חורבן is worse than the one before, the world is held up by the קדושה דסידרא and the יהא שמיה רבא after learning. Where there is 'סדר', light comes out of the darkness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is why the קדושה in ובא לציון and the קדיש after a public lesson are treated as so important: the גמרא says the world's survival depends on them.

steps.title: Lost טהרה took away taste and smell, and lost מעשר took away the richness of grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about dew and fruit losing their blessing. It brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains the cause: lost טהרה removed taste and smell, and lost מעשר removed the richness of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: dew no longer falls for a blessing, and fruit has lost its taste. A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: the loss of טהרה took away taste and smell, and the loss of מעשר took away the fatness of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה about fruit losing its taste. It brings a ברייתא that names two spiritual causes for this loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that fruit lost its taste. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds the reason, and splits it in two: losing טהרה hurt taste and smell, while not separating מעשר hurt the richness of grain. Food's physical quality is tied to how holy the people are.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithes, the part of the crop that must be set aside
The fatness or richness of grain
It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next story, which shows that a person with טהרה can still sense fragrance the rest of us have lost.

phrases.english: And dew has not fallen for a blessing
and the taste of fruit was taken away, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Purity, once lost, took away taste and smell;
tithes, once neglected, took away the fatness of grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה after the discussion about each day being worse than the last.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost טהרה removed taste and smell from food; unseparated מעשר removed the richness of grain.

steps.title: רב הונא's son smells the hidden fragrant date
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא wraps a fragrant date in his cloth. His son רבה smells it, and רב הונא says this shows רבה has טהרה, then gives him the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא found a fragrant date. He took it and wrapped it in his cloth. His son רבה came and said, 'I smell the smell of a fragrant date.' רב הונא said, 'My son, there is purity in you,' and gave it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the ברייתא's idea in real life: someone with טהרה can still smell what others cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said lost טהרה took away smell. Here רבה smells a date that is wrapped up and hidden, so רב הונא concludes that רבה must have טהרה. The story backs up the link between purity and smell.

keyTerms.meaning: A fragrant, pleasant kind of date

phrases.english: Rav Huna found a fragrant date,
took it, and wrapped it in his shawl.
Rabba his son came and said to him:
I smell the smell of a fragrant date.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנִי, טׇהֳרָה יֵשׁ בְּךָ.
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, there is purity in you.
He gave it to him.
phrases.notes: רב הונא handed the date to his son רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אַשְׁכַּח תּוֹמַרְתָּא דְּחִינוּנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ברייתא's link between טהרה and smell in a real story.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that טהרה keeps the sense of fragrance alive.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה smelled a wrapped-up date, and רב הונא said this showed his טהרה.

steps.title: רבה gives the date to his own son, and love flows downward
steps.stepSummary: רבה's son אבא arrives, and רבה gives him the date. רב הונא says this both pleased him and pained him. The גמרא links this to a folk saying: a father's love goes to his sons, and the sons' love goes to their own sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile אבא, רבה's son, came. רבה took the date and gave it to him. רב הונא said to רבה, 'My son, you made my heart happy, and you set my teeth on edge.' This is what people say: a father's love is for his sons; the sons' love is for their own sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבה passes the date to his own son instead of keeping it or giving it back to his father. The גמרא sums it up with a common saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא was happy to see his son's טהרה, but hurt that רבה cared more for his own son than for his father. The folk saying explains that this is natural: love goes down the generations more than it goes back up.

keyTerms.meaning: You set my teeth on edge, meaning you hurt me
That people say, a folk saying

steps.confusionAlert: There are three generations here: רב הונא (grandfather), רבה (his son), and אבא (רבה's son). 'He said to him: my son' in phrase 3 is רב הונא speaking to רבה.

phrases.english: Meanwhile Abba, his son, came,
phrases.notes: This is רבה's son, so he is רב הונא's grandson.

phrases.english: he took it and gave it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנִי, שִׂמַּחְתָּ אֶת לִבִּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you made my heart happy,
and you set my teeth on edge.
This is what people say:
The love of a father is for the sons;
the love of the sons is for the sons they have.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story and turns it to a new lesson about how love flows between generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A parent's love naturally goes to his children more than back up to his own parent.

steps.title: A grandson raised by his grandfather says he is not his son
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב raised his daughter's son, רב יעקב. When the grandson grew up and was asked for water, he said he was not his son. The גמרא links this to a folk saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב took care of רב יעקב, his daughter's son. When he grew up, רב אחא said to him, 'Give me water to drink.' He answered, 'I am not your son.' This is what people say: Raise him, raise him, and in the end he says, 'I am your daughter's son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with the same message: love and duty do not flow back up the generations the way they flow down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after being raised by his grandfather, the grandson felt he had no duty to serve him like a son serves a father. The folk saying makes the point: you can put all your effort into a grandchild, and he may still see himself as only a daughter's son.
steps.whatToRemember: Both stories teach the same folk wisdom: a person's love goes down to his own children more than up to his parents or grandparents.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אִיטַּפַּל בֵּיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov took care of
Rav Yaakov, the son of his daughter.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי גְדַל אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַשְׁקְיַין מַיָּא.
phrases.english: When he grew up, he said to him: Give me water to drink.
He said to him: I am not your son.
And this is what people say:
Raise, raise, and he says: I am your daughter's son.
phrases.notes: Here רַבִּי means 'raise' (bring up a child), not 'my teacher.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אִיטַּפַּל בֵּיהּ בְּרַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר בְּרַתֵּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that repeats the lesson of the previous step, again closed with a folk saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandchild raised by a grandparent may still not feel the duty a son has to his father.

steps.title: New משנה: decrees against bridegrooms' crowns and drums in the war of אספסיינוס
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: during the war of אספסיינוס, the חכמים banned bridegrooms' crowns and the drum.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In the war of אספסיינוס, the חכמים made decrees against bridegrooms' crowns and against the drum.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה that lists decrees made in times of national sorrow. This is the first item on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the war of אספסיינוס, the חכמים cut back signs of joy at weddings: bridegrooms could no longer wear crowns, and drums were no longer played. The גמרא will go on to explain these decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Vespasian, the Roman general who fought against ירושלים

phrases.english: MISHNA:
In the war of Vespasian
they made a decree against the crowns of bridegrooms
and against the drum.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפוּלְמוּס שֶׁל אַסְפַּסְיָינוּס גָּזְרוּ עַל עַטְרוֹת חֲתָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the stories that explained the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the war of אספסיינוס, the חכמים banned bridegrooms' crowns and drums.

steps.title: Decrees made in the war of טיטוס
steps.stepSummary: During the war of טיטוס, the חכמים banned brides' crowns and banned teaching one's son Greek.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the war of טיטוס they decreed against brides' crowns, and that a person should not teach his son Greek.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing the decrees made during the wars with Rome. This time it is the war of טיטוס, which brought two new bans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 banned bridegrooms' crowns during the war of אספסיינוס. Now, in a later war, the ban grows to cover brides' crowns too. A second, different ban is added: not teaching one's son Greek.

keyTerms.meaning: Titus, the Roman general who destroyed the second בית המקדש

phrases.english: In the war of Titus
they decreed against the crowns of brides,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ יְווֹנִית.
phrases.english: and that a person should not teach his son Greek.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפוּלְמוּס שֶׁל טִיטוּס גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of wartime decrees from step 21, moving to the next war.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the war of טיטוס: no brides' crowns, and no teaching one's son Greek.

steps.title: The bride's carriage: banned, then permitted
steps.stepSummary: In the last war they banned a bride from riding in a covered carriage inside the city. Later, רבותינו permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the last war they decreed that a bride may not go out in a covered carriage inside the city. But our Sages permitted a bride to go out in a covered carriage inside the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the decree from the last war, about a bride's carriage. It then reports that a later group of sages lifted that decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier decrees, this one did not stay in place. רבותינו later permitted the bride's carriage again. The wording of the permission repeats the wording of the ban exactly, which makes it clear that the very same thing became allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A covered carriage or litter that carries the bride
Our Sages: a later court that lifted the decree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop reading at the ban. The final word in the משנה is that רבותינו permitted the bride's carriage again.

phrases.english: In the last war
they decreed that the bride may not go out
in a palanquin inside the city,
phrases.notes: A palanquin is a covered carriage carried on poles, with the bride sitting inside.

phrases.english: but our Sages permitted
that the bride may go out
in a palanquin inside the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפוּלְמוּס הָאַחֲרוֹן גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the third war in the list, and adds that a later group of sages lifted this decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on a bride's carriage from the last war was later lifted by רבותינו.
steps.whatToRemember: There were three wars and three sets of decrees: אספסיינוס (grooms' crowns and the drum), טיטוס (brides' crowns and Greek), and the last war (the bride's carriage, later permitted).

steps.title: Qualities that ended when great sages died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new list. When רבי מאיר, בן עזאי, בן זומא, רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא בן דוסא died, the quality each was known for ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי מאיר died, the tellers of parables ended. When בן עזאי died, the diligent learners ended. When בן זומא died, the expounders of verses ended. When רבי עקיבא died, the honor of the Torah ended. When רבי חנינא בן דוסא died, the men of wondrous deeds ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic. It lists great sages, and for each one it names the special quality that disappeared when he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line follows the same pattern: 'from when X died, Y ended.' Every sage stands for one special strength. רבי מאיר is linked to parables, בן עזאי to hard work in learning, בן זומא to explaining verses, רבי עקיבא to the honor of the Torah, and רבי חנינא בן דוסא to wondrous deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time that he died
They ceased or came to an end
People who learn with great diligence
Those who expound the meaning of verses
Men of action, known for wondrous deeds

phrases.english: From when Rabbi Meir died
the tellers of parables ceased.
From when ben Azzai died
the diligent ceased.
From when ben Zoma died
the expounders ceased.
From when Rabbi Akiva died
the honor of the Torah ceased.
From when Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa died
the men of wondrous deeds ceased.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי מֵאִיר בָּטְלוּ מוֹשְׁלֵי מְשָׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wartime decrees and opens a new list in the משנה, about qualities lost when sages died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each great sage carried a special quality, and that quality ended when he died.

steps.title: רבי יוסי the Small and why he had that name
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוסי קטנתא died, the חסידים ended. The משנה explains that he was called 'the Small' because he was the smallest of the חסידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוסי קטנתא died, the pious ones were no more. Why was he called 'קטנתא'? Because he was the smallest of the pious ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with רבי יוסי קטנתא. The משנה then stops to explain his unusual nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks and answers its own short question: why is he called 'the Small'? The answer is that he was the least of the חסידים. Even so, once he died, there were no חסידים left at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They stopped or were no more

phrases.english: From when Rabbi Yosei the Small died
the pious were no more.
And why was he called "the Small"?
Because he was the smallest of the pious.
phrases.notes: He means the least important among the pious men, not short in height.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ קְטֹנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from step 24 and adds a short explanation of a sage's name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the death of רבי יוסי קטנתא, the least of the חסידים, the חסידים came to an end.

steps.title: The list ends with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי through רבי
steps.stepSummary: The list continues with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי (the glory of wisdom), רבן גמליאל הזקן (the honor of the Torah, purity and separation), רבי ישמעאל בן פיאבי (the glory of the כהונה), and רבי (humility and fear of sin).
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן יוחנן בן זכאי died, the glory of wisdom ended. When רבן גמליאל הזקן died, the honor of the Torah ended, and purity and separation died. When רבי ישמעאל בן פיאבי died, the glory of the כהונה ended. When רבי died, humility and fear of sin ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of great sages and the qualities that ended with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These last entries follow the same pattern as before. רבן גמליאל הזקן is linked to more than one quality: the honor of the Torah, plus purity and separation. The list closes with רבי, who stands for humility and fear of sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The shine or glory of wisdom
Separation: holding back from worldly pleasures

steps.whatToRemember: The second list in the משנה pairs each great sage with one special quality, and says that quality ended when he died.

phrases.english: From when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai died
the glory of wisdom ceased.
From when Rabban Gamliel the Elder died
the honor of the Torah ceased,
and purity and separation died.
From when Rabbi Yishmael ben Pavi died
the glory of the priesthood ceased.
From when Rabbi died
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: humility and fear of sin ceased.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, so read it as בטלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בָּטַל זִיו הַחׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of sages and lost qualities that began in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wisdom, Torah honor, purity, the glory of the כהונה, humility and fear of sin each ended with the death of the sage who embodied it.

steps.title: רבי פנחס בן יאיר: What society lost when the בית המקדש fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. In it, רבי פנחס בן יאיר says that after the בית המקדש was destroyed, the חברים and the בני חורין were shamed, men of good deeds dwindled, violent people and smooth-talkers took control, and nobody searched for or asked about the right way to live.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The Sages taught: רבי פנחס בן יאיר says: From the time the בית המקדש was destroyed, the חברים and the free men were put to shame and covered their heads. Men of action dwindled, and violent men and smooth-talkers gained the upper hand. No one seeks, no one asks, and no one inquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its own discussion by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי פנחס בן יאיר describes how society went downhill once the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed great people whose deaths ended a special quality. This ברייתא adds a wider picture of the whole society. The respected, decent people lost their standing, and the strong and the loud took over. Even the drive to seek out and ask about the right path disappeared.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Sages taught": the opening formula for a ברייתא
Members of a circle known for careful observance and Torah learning
Free men, people of good standing
Men of action: people known for good deeds
Strong-armed people who get their way by force
Smooth-talkers who get their way with words

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says:
From the time the Temple was destroyed
the haverim and the free men were put to shame,
and they covered their heads,
and men of action dwindled,
and the strong-armed gained the upper hand
and the smooth-talkers,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דּוֹרֵשׁ וְאֵין מְבַקֵּשׁ וְאֵין שׁוֹאֵל,
phrases.english: and no one seeks, no one asks, and no one inquires,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion. It widens the משנה's theme of lost qualities into a picture of how society as a whole declined after the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, the respected and righteous lost their standing, the violent and the smooth-talking took over, and no one searched for the right path.

steps.title: Only our Father in Heaven is left to rely on
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר ends his description with a cry: with everyone else failing, the only one we can lean on is our Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Upon whom can we rely? Only upon our Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes רבי פנחס בן יאיר's list. After showing that society has collapsed, he concludes that we can rely only on ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every human support was taken away in the previous step: the leaders, the doers and even the people asking questions. The natural result is that only ה׳ remains to depend on. The line turns a sad description into a statement of faith.

keyTerms.meaning: To lean on or rely upon

steps.whatToRemember: The refrain "עַל מִי לָנוּ לְהִשָּׁעֵן עַל אָבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם" closes each description of decline: when all human support is gone, we rely on ה׳.

phrases.english: Upon whom can we rely?
Upon our Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מִי לָנוּ לְהִשָּׁעֵן עַל אָבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list from step 27 with its emotional and spiritual conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With all human leadership failing, the only true support left is our Father in Heaven.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר הגדול: Each level of learned people slid down a rung
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר הגדול begins a parallel statement. Since the חורבן, scholars have become like teachers of children, those teachers like synagogue attendants, those attendants like the unlearned, and the unlearned... His list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the scholars began to be like the teachers of children, the teachers of children like the synagogue attendants, the synagogue attendants like the עמי הארץ, and the עמי הארץ...
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא, רבי אליעזר הגדול, gives his own description of the decline after the חורבן. The amud ends in the middle of his list, so the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פנחס בן יאיר described society as a whole. רבי אליעזר הגדול focuses on Torah knowledge and shows it as a ladder where every rung dropped one level. The top scholars now stand where simple teachers used to be, and so on all the way down.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribes, here meaning teachers of young children

steps.confusionAlert: Here חַזָּנַיָּא does not mean a cantor who leads the davening, as the word is used today. It means the synagogue attendant who takes care of practical tasks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
the scholars began to be like the scribes,
phrases.notes: These "scribes" are the people who teach young children.

phrases.english: and the scribes like the beadles,
and the beadles like the ignorant people,
and the ignorant people...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel description of decline after the חורבן. This one focuses on how each level of Torah knowledge slipped down a step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, every level of learned people has dropped one rung: scholars to children's teachers, teachers to attendants, attendants to the unlearned, and so on.
